chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man came as a pilgrim but missed the Hajj, and he had not performed Tawaf. He said: He stays with the people as a Harami (one in the state of Ihram for Hajj) during the Days of Tashriq, and there is no Umrah in them. When they end, he performs Tawaf with the House and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, and he becomes Muhsin (free from Ihram restrictions), and Hajj is incumbent upon him next year. He enters Ihram from where he entered Ihram.

key_terms.أَحَلّ: Became Muhsin, free from the restrictions of Ihram
key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: The Days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.حَرَاماً: One in the state of Ihram for Hajj, specifically referring to the Qarini or Mufrid who stays in Ihram
key_terms.سَعَى: Performed Sa'i, the walking between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.طَافَ: Performed Tawaf, the circumambulation of the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if he arrives in Mecca in Ihram but misses the Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar addresses the specific case of 'Hajj al-Qiran' or incomplete Hajj where the pilgrim remains in the state of Ihram during the Days of Tashriq (11th–13th Dhu al-Hijjah) to await the completion of rituals. By delaying the Tawaf and Sa'i until after these days, the pilgrim avoids the penalty of an Umrah and preserves the validity of the current year's Hajj, a nuance highlighted by Shia jurists to distinguish between mere delay and actual omission. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining the continuity of the Hajj state to minimize ritual burden while ensuring the obligation is fulfilled in the subsequent year.
